The compound is a di-substituted benzene ring with 8 total carbons, an aromatic-halogen bond, and a carbonyl group. The substituents must account for 2 carbons (benzene has 6). The 1H NMR data in options A and B both show a para-disubstituted aromatic pattern (two doublets, 2H each), but the chemical shifts differ.

Option A has an aldehyde proton at 9.9 ppm and a CH2 singlet at 3.7 ppm, suggesting a –CH2CHO substituent. However, the aromatic protons at 7.8 and 7.6 ppm are too deshielded for a ring bearing only a –CH2CHO group (which is not directly conjugated to the ring); such protons typically appear around 7.1–7.3 ppm.

Option B has a methyl singlet at 2.3 ppm, consistent with a –COCH3 (acetyl) substituent directly attached to the ring. The acetyl group strongly deshields the ortho protons, giving signals around 7.8–7.9 ppm, while the meta protons (ortho to halogen) appear slightly upfield (~7.4–7.6 ppm). The given shifts (7.8 and 7.6 ppm) match this pattern well. Options C and D lack the required aromatic proton pattern and are incorrect.

Thus, the correct 1H NMR data corresponds to 4-haloacetophenone.

Answer: B
